A1.justification: Both PDFs present RNG: Relightable Neural Gaussians and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material. Existing content can be matched across layout changes and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original relighting experiments in Tables 1–2, component ablations, and supplementary novel-view synthesis results in Table 3.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results and adds a shadow cue ablation example in supplementary Figure 13.

M1.justification: The neural Gaussian representation, conditioned decoder, shadow mapping, depth refinement, losses, and two-stage optimization remain unchanged. Section 3.3 clarifies depth weights and shadow cue notation without establishing a changed computation.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same real and synthetic scene coverage, point-light and environment-light relighting, and fixed-light novel-view synthesis. The added Cat example examines an existing component on an already represented scene, without introducing a distinct task or environment.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain NRHints and GS3 for point lighting, GS-IR and Relightable 3D Gaussian for environment lighting, and vanilla SH-based 3DGS for supplementary novel-view synthesis. Table 2 merely abbreviates Relightable 3D Gaussian as RelightableGS.

E3.justification: Reported resolution, view budget, training schedule, model configuration, and PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics remain unchanged. v5 removes the camera-pose optimization disclosure but states no replacement setting; this establishes a documentation loss rather than a changed protocol. Figure 13 extends the existing shadow cue ablation.

E4.justification: New supplementary Figure 13 examines the shadow cue contribution on Cat using renderings, enlarged dark regions, a reference, and a cue visualization. Existing component, depth-refinement, shading-strategy, moving-light, and network-size analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The new example adds point estimates without changing uncertainty reporting practices.

E6.justification: New Figure 13 reports PSNR 17.1941 without the shadow cue and 25.4496 with it, alongside improved dark-region detail and shadow boundaries. Tables 1–3 and matched existing figure results retain their numerical values; the network-size results are only moved and renumbered.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8) and the depth-scaling assumption are retained. Calling alpha_i a Gaussian ray response clarifies its existing meaning in Section 3.1, while V = |PQ| restates the previously described shadow distance. No new mathematical derivation or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same relighting capabilities, component contributions, shadow-quality claims, and efficiency claims of approximately 1.3 hours training and 60 fps rendering. The added ablation supports an existing claim.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 newly explains that normalizing the depth proxy reduces background leakage in semitransparent regions. Section 4.5 also explicitly connects depth refinement to the retained geometry limitation; the existing accuracy, geometry, and reflective-material limitations remain.

D1.justification: v5 adds a project page address to the abstract but removes Section 4.2's statement that camera-pose optimization was disabled for NRHints and GS3. Hardware, hyperparameters, and training details remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the resources available through the new address.

R1.justification: The same 33 cited works and substantive research positioning are retained, including the relationships to NRHints and GS3. Reference differences are limited to typesetting.

P1.justification: Localized edits clarify Section 3.3, shorten the supplementary-material signpost, update affiliations, and add acknowledgements. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v5 adds Figure 13, compacts Figure 6's legend, and relocates Figure 8 within its page. Supplementary Table 3 is repositioned, and the existing network-size and relighting figures move and become Figures 14–15. The overall two-column design and existing visual content are retained.

improvement.justification: The added Cat ablation in Figure 13 modestly strengthens evidence for a central component, while Section 3.3 improves the explanation of depth weighting and normalization. Removing the camera-pose optimization disclosure weakens reproducibility and partly offsets these gains. The unchanged main results and claims support only a limited overall improvement.
